stemMd:
Most commercial vanilla flavouring is synthesised in a factory rather than extracted from an orchid pod. The synthetic molecule is chemically identical to the one the pod produces, so no laboratory test of that molecule alone can tell the two sources apart. ______ trained tasters can usually distinguish them, because a cured pod also carries dozens of minor compounds that the synthetic version lacks.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanationMd:
Transitions are decided by the logical relationship between the sentence before the blank and the sentence after it, so state both in your own words first.

Before: a lab test of the molecule cannot separate synthetic from natural vanilla. After: trained tasters usually can. The second fact runs against what the first leads you to expect, so the relationship is contrast. "Nevertheless" marks exactly that.

Check by reading the sentence aloud with your choice in place and asking whether the second statement is a surprise given the first. It is — which rules out any transition of similarity, illustration or consequence.

distractorRationale.b: This signals an illustration, but tasters distinguishing the two sources is not an example of a test failing to distinguish them. It is the opposite outcome, so the relationship is contrast rather than exemplification.
distractorRationale.d: This signals that the second statement matches the first. Here the second statement reports a success where the first reported a failure, so treating them as parallel misreads the passage.
distractorRationale.a: This signals cause and effect. The inability of a lab test to tell the two apart does not cause tasters to succeed; if anything it makes their success unexpected.

accessibilityText: Choose the transition that best fills the blank at the start of the third sentence, which contrasts a laboratory test that cannot distinguish synthetic from natural vanilla with trained tasters who usually can.
